title: A response can change
hook: An initial response and a later response can differ.

knows: Animals can respond to cues and conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy test, response A stays the same across practice, while response B improves after practice. Which pattern is consistent with learning?

misconception: The stated evidence implies a different interpretation or a universal conclusion.
objective: In a toy test, response A stays the same across practice, while response B improves after practice. Which pattern is consistent with learning?

claims.text: In a toy test, response A stays the same across practice, while response B improves after practice. Which pattern is consistent with learning? Panel A shows the same stipulated response on each trial. Panel B shows a response changing after practice. That change is consistent with learning, although fatigue, growth or other factors would need controls before concluding why.
claims.source: Unverified research lead; confirm exact claim and species with an independent source reviewer: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology ; where applicable consult a specialist source. The illustrated observations and values are stipulated toy examples.

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative model and do not depict observed data.
A trained animal’s performance changes across practice. What is one possibility to investigate? A change after practice is consistent with learning but does not prove its cause.
